# fortiappseccloud_waf_known_bots

Configures known bots for one FortiAppSec Cloud application using the static app endpoint `/waf/apps/{ep_id}/known_bots`. Set `template = false` and provide `configs` to manage settings directly. Set `template = true` and omit `configs` to inherit this module from the application's attached WAF template.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_known_bots` resource for an application endpoint. Template-level settings are managed by `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_known_bots`.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_known_bots" "example" {
  ep_id    = fortiappseccloud_waf_app.example.ep_id
  template = false

  configs {
    status           = true
    bad_bots         = true
    bad_bots_action  = "block_period"
    good_bots_action = "bypass"

    bad_bots_list {
      item {
        cat    = "DoS"
        status = true
        allow_list {
          item {
            value = "AB"
          }
        }
      }
    }

    good_bots_list {
      item {
        cat    = "Known Search Engines"
        status = true
        deny_list {
          item {
            value = "Ask"
          }
        }
      }
    }

    exception_list {
      item {
        concatenate_type = "AND"
        match_target     = "COOKIE"
        operator         = "REGEXP_MATCH"
        value_name       = "session_id"
        value_check      = true
        value            = "terraform-matrix"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Import

Import using the application `ep_id`:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_known_bots.example application-endpoint-id
```

The first read after import hydrates all ownership wrappers when `template = false`.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
